title: Low-Level Cryptoparameter Manipulation (Nonce Reuse)
pattern: Writing custom cryptologic that exposes low-level parameters (such as nonces or initialization vectors) to application developers, leading to static nonce assignments.
why_bad: Reusing a nonce in Galois Counter Mode (GCM) destroys its authenticity guarantees. An adversary observing two payloads encrypted with the same nonce can recover the authentication key, causing complete system failure.
detection: Static string literals or array constants passed to initialization parameters for nonces or IVs in standard crypto APIs.
fix: Utilize high-level, correct-by-construction cryptographic libraries (like Tink) that abstract parameter management and prevent nonce reuse by design.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 6, p. 118.
